---
title: "Selected campaign report"
engine: knitr
---

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| results: asis
source("R/reporting.R")
report <- benchmark_report_read()
cat("Campaign: **", report$manifest$campaign_id, "**\n\n", sep = "")
cat("Frozen execution identity: `", report$manifest$identity_id, "`\n\n", sep = "")
cat("Execution revision: `", report$manifest$identity$code$revision, "`; dirty: ",
    report$manifest$identity$code$dirty, "\n\n", sep = "")
print(knitr::kable(report$availability, format = "pipe"))
```

## Reading this report

This is a new campaign-specific reporting implementation, not a recovery of the
historical figure generators. Historical published results remain separate in
`docs/` and are not inputs to this report. Synthetic fixtures demonstrate the
reporting route only; they are not benchmark evidence.

Every completed attempt is retained in the [attempt ledger](tables/attempts.csv),
including failures, skips, validation outcomes, warm-ups, diagnostics,
comparability labels, and monitoring coverage. Missing or corrupt raw records
block the build. Planned but unattempted measurement slots appear in summaries.

For each tool/task/run/phase/repetition, the latest attempt by the precise
`started.rds` timestamp is selected (lexical attempt ID breaks exact ties).
A failed final retry does not fall back to an earlier success. Warm-ups and
superseded attempts cannot contribute samples. Eligible timings require recorded
execution success, passed artifact validation or an explicitly accepted surface
exception, and finite elapsed time of at
least 0.1 seconds. Short timings are flagged without changing execution status.
Accepted exceptions retain their diagnostics, contribute to descriptive timings
and `n_accepted_exception`, and never count as passed numerical comparisons.
Means, medians, ranges and sample standard deviations use one selected eligible
attempt per repetition; a single sample has **NA**, not zero, SD.

Timing uses the immutable monitor-bound subsecond workload epochs where present;
otherwise raw CSV timestamps have only second resolution. The ledger identifies
the precision per attempt. The report does not invent subsecond precision.
Workload time includes tool I/O/computation/persistence, not setup, validation,
cleanup or cooldown. Complex timings are actual end-to-end calls only.
No sum of independent basic tasks is labeled sequential execution or CHM.

Tool-specific timings with non-comparable/unknown contracts are descriptive,
not cross-tool speedup claims. `n_comparable` additionally requires a matched
definition/group and passed validation; this is not general equivalence or
real-input acceptance. Storage names and nominal tile size/density come only
from standard `ALS_<tile>_<density>_<cores>_<input>_<output>` run IDs.
Nonstandard IDs retain their timings but have unknown dimensions. Storage/tile
views retain run strata and do not claim causal comparisons across different
datasets or hardware; input checksums and mounts are in the frozen manifest.

CPU is Linux whole-machine busy percent (0–100); RAM used is
`MemTotal - MemAvailable` in bytes, **not process RSS**. Only full-coverage,
eligible measurements enter utilization aggregates. Partial/disabled/unavailable
monitoring stays explicit in the ledger; no missing value becomes zero.
Per-attempt means are duration-weighted over the timed interval; reported
campaign means and sample SDs weight eligible repetitions equally.
Peaks are maxima of overlapping samples. Unrelated activity and monitor overhead
contribute; brief peaks can be missed. Historical Windows counters are not pooled.

## All attempts and exclusions

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| results: asis
columns <- c("task_id", "run_id", "tool", "phase", "repetition_id", "attempt_id",
             "execution_status", "validation_status", "exclusion", "diagnostic",
             "validation_diagnostic", "comparison_note", "monitoring_status",
             "monitoring_coverage_fraction", "timing_precision")
columns <- intersect(columns, names(report$attempts))
print(knitr::kable(report$attempts[columns], format = "pipe"))
```
